Perfect! All 28 tests pass across all 8 test files. Here's what I fixed:

## Summary

I fixed two failing tests in the frai-core test suite:

1. **`src/finetune/governance.test.js`** — The test was trying to import `APPROVAL_STATUSES` as a named export, but it wasn't being re-exported from the finetune module. I added an `export` statement to re-export it (and related schema constants) from `./schema.js`.

2. **`src/eval/index.test.js`** — The `toxicityMetric` function has a signature of `toxicityMetric(outputs, bannedTerms)`, but it was being called with `toxicityMetric(outputs, references)` in the test. This caused references to be used as banned terms, flagging all outputs as toxic (score=0). I wrapped the function in `DEFAULT_METRICS` so it only receives the outputs parameter.

Both fixes maintain backward compatibility and preserve all existing public exports (verified via module inspection).

Perfect! All 28 tests pass across all 8 test files. Here's what I fixed:

## Summary

I fixed two failing tests in the frai-core test suite:

1. **`src/finetune/governance.test.js`** — The test was trying to import `APPROVAL_STATUSES` as a named export, but it wasn't being re-exported from the finetune module. I added an `export` statement to re-export it (and related schema constants) from `./schema.js`.

2. **`src/eval/index.test.js`** — The `toxicityMetric` function has a signature of `toxicityMetric(outputs, bannedTerms)`, but it was being called with `toxicityMetric(outputs, references)` in the test. This caused references to be used as banned terms, flagging all outputs as toxic (score=0). I wrapped the function in `DEFAULT_METRICS` so it only receives the outputs parameter.

Both fixes maintain backward compatibility and preserve all existing public exports (verified via module inspection).
